subject: Clarify Exhibit Transition + Ops Guardrails for Order Form Amendment
messages:
From: Anna Cole <anna.cole@nimbushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: exhibit F transition + ops guardrails for Order Form amendment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete change request so we can finish approval paperwork. Two asks from our side:

1) Move the current Exhibit F (throughput transition plan) into the Order Form as an explicit schedule so our SREs have a defined cutover window and acceptance criteria. We want the rollback window and pre-cutover smoke test defined.

2) Add a short "Ops Guardrails" annex (1 page) that documents required logging/audit levels, minimum KV cache retention for warm starts, and a fallback routing policy to a lower-tier model during sustained queueing. This isn't a security carveout, it's an operational requirement so our on-call can triage fast.

We attached a rough ops-guardrails doc and a price-impact matrix — procurement flagged that moving Exhibit F into the Order Form might change the fee schedule. Can you confirm whether that triggers a pricing adjustment or falls under implementation credits?

Target: we'd like to get an executable amendment signed by 4/22 to meet our Q2 go-live.

Appreciate the help — cc'ing procurement.

Best,
Anna
Procurement Lead, Nimbus Health

Attachments: ops-guardrails-summary-20270414.pdf, price-impact-matrix-20270414.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cole <anna.cole@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exhibit F transition + ops guardrails for Order Form amendment

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Quick read-through and next steps below.

Summary of what we'll do:
- Legal will scope whether embedding Exhibit F into the Order Form constitutes a commercial change that affects the fee schedule (Marcus will lead).
- Product/Implementations will author a tightened Exhibit F with cutover/rollback templates and explicit acceptance criteria (Connor).
- Finance will run the price-impact matrix and propose either an implementation credit or a nominal one-time fee if there is an ongoing SLA change (Laura).

Immediate asks from us to you:
1) Can you confirm the target cutover duration (hours) and whether Nimbus wants an automated rollback after X minutes of degraded latency, or a manual rollback?
2) Any regulatory constraints on KV cache retention (e.g., must not persist > Y days) or is this an internal ops preference?

I'll loop Marcus and Laura to own legal/finance review. We'll aim to produce a redlined amendment for your review by Friday (4/16) so you have time to circulate internally before the 4/22 signature target.

Thanks — Kimberly
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: exhibit-F-transition-draft-v1.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exhibit F transition + ops guardrails for Order Form amendment

Kimberly / Connor —

I reviewed Anna's attachments. Initial legal read: migrating an operational schedule from an appendix to the Order Form itself can be treated as a "non-substantive" operationalization if the commercial terms (billing bands, committed throughput, SLA targets) are unchanged. If we include explicit rollback automation and a fallback routing policy to a different model class that introduces a sustained change in expected throughput, that may be treated as a commercial change and require a fee adjustment.

Action items for legal:
- I'll prepare two redline tracks: (A) Operationalization-only edits that preserve fees and include a statement that Exhibit F is for scheduling/ops only; (B) Operationalization + SLA/automation edits that include a price-impact appendix and an option for one-time implementation fee.
- Connor, we'll need a 1-page engineering impact note describing whether fallback routing could materially change GPU usage under expected load (ballpark % uplift). Laura, please slot for a quick price check.

Timeline: I can get both redline tracks to Kimberly by end of day Thursday (4/15) if we have Connor's engineering note by EOD today.

Marcus
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Anna Cole <anna.cole@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exhibit F transition + ops guardrails for Order Form amendment

Marcus / Kimberly / Anna —

Quick engineering impact note (summary):
- Fallback routing to a lower-capacity model during sustained queueing is expected to increase total token-equivalent compute by ~6-11% during peak retention windows because of extra reroutes and shorter context lengths on fallback.
- Automated rollback (after N minutes of latency degradation) reduces manual toil but may increase short-term token spikes during failback. We recommend an automated rollback threshold with a 10-minute cool-down to avoid flip-flop.
- KV cache retention: default 24 hours is fine for Nimbus's stated use case. If Nimbus requires >72 hours that may increase memory footprint and affect instance sizing (we can support but will advise pricing uplift).

I will attach a short one-page note into the Drive folder and flag the likely price band impact for Laura.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
